No driver implementation was attempted after this blocker. Package directory contents at the last run: task.json, check-report.json and this RESULT.json.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Confirmed the author's block: the reviewer's gate run fails G1.CLONE_MODIFIED (besides the missing-file findings of an unauthored package) because the clone's submodule workspace/vendor/unitree_mujoco has a modified tracked file, unitree_robots/go2w/assets/terrain.STL, whose modification time (2026-10-13) predates wave C; the reviewer ran no git and did not touch the clone. PROMPT.md hard rule 1 prescribes SDK_BUG for a modified clone, but this is a clone-integrity problem, not an SDK defect: the same relative path is the known unitree_mujoco file of CODEX-HANDOFF rule 11, here in grove-g1's vendored fork (the two files differ), and only an operator restore from the pinned commit unblocks the card. No driver was written, so nothing else could be reviewed; the reviewer changed no authored file, and the gate re-run rewrote check-report.json with the same findings. For the human reviewer: Grove-G1 is a ROS 2 Jazzy autonomy stack for the Unitree G1 humanoid (Nav2, MoveIt, approach, pick, place and posture action servers, a learned locomotion controller that owns the legs over rt/lowcmd). README.md:8-11 says the same hardware interface, navigation and control code run unchanged on the real G1 after a change of DDS domain and network interface, and README.md:84-85 says commanding rt/lowcmd means owning balance with no onboard controller underneath. A future package bound to these endpoints is only as simulated as the operator's DDS domain: rate it by the real humanoid's hazards (R2; MHS/spec/04-safety.md:71-76) unless the deployment is isolated, and find a source-backed stop (g1_controllers has freeze and safety controllers) before any actuation is accepted.
